explanation:
## How the puzzle works

**What the grid is made of.** Every input contains a few 2×2 blocks of mixed colours on a black (0) background. The output keeps every block unchanged and adds a solid "tail" of colour 3 directly beneath each block. The tail is always two cells wide, the same width as the block.

**What sets the tail length.** Counting the distinct colours inside each block matches the tail length in every case:

| Pair | Block cells | Distinct colours | Tail rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4,8 / 9,4 | 3 | 3 |
| 1 | 2,1 / 1,2 | 2 | 2 |
| 2 | 9,9 / 6,6 | 2 | 2 |
| 2 | 8,4 / 7,7 | 3 | 3 (rows 7–9, reaching the border) |
| 3 | 2,4 / 6,7 | 4 | 4 |
| 3 | 9,8 / 8,9 | 2 | 2 |
| 3 | 7,6 / 6,6 | 2 | 2 |

The fact sheet confirms this. The only colour transition is 0→3, and every added segment starts in the row just below a block. So the rule is: under each block, paint `len(set(block colours))` rows of colour 3. Stop at the grid edge, and only paint background cells.

**Finding the blocks.** Multicolour 4-connected objects pick out each 2×2 block as one unit. In every grid, including the test, the blocks are separate from each other even diagonally.

**Applying it to the test.**
- Block at rows 1–2, cols 0–1 (1,1 / 2,1) has 2 colours, so 3s go in rows 3–4, cols 0–1.
- Block at rows 1–2, cols 6–7 (2,9 / 1,6) has 4 colours, so 3s go in rows 3–6, cols 6–7.
- Block at rows 3–4, cols 3–4 (4,7 / 8,4) has 3 colours, so 3s go in rows 5–7, cols 3–4.

None of these tails overlap a block or another tail.

**Construction stages.** The program emits one canvas per tail, then the final canvas.
code:
def transform(grid):
    g = np.array(grid)
    bg = background(g)
    out = g.copy()
    H, W = g.shape
    objs = objects(g, bg=bg, multicolour=True)
    for o in objs:
        y0, x0, y1, x1 = o["box"]
        cols = set(int(g[y, x]) for y, x in o["cells"])
        n = len(cols)
        for y in range(y1 + 1, min(H, y1 + 1 + n)):
            for x in range(x0, x1 + 1):
                if out[y, x] == bg:
                    out[y, x] = 3
        emit(out, f"Block at rows {y0}-{y1}, cols {x0}-{x1} has {n} distinct colours, so draw a {n}-row tail of 3 beneath it.")
    emit(out, "All blocks have their tails; final output.")
    return out
